channel.title: SecuBuzz · Cybersecurity News Briefs
channel.description: Fast, factual 60-word cybersecurity briefs and CISA KEV alerts for security professionals.

item.title: Red Hat Satellite 6.17.13 receives critical async update
item.description: Red Hat Satellite 6.17.13 for RHEL 9 contains critical flaws that could let attackers compromise satellite management. The flaws are rated CVSS 9.0+, exposing remote code execution paths that bypass authentication and grant full control over satellite services. Red Hat recommends installing the provided patch immediately; administrators should also verify satellite configuration and apply any additional hardening guidelines.

item.title: Red Hat Satellite 6.18.11 receives critical async update
item.description: Red Hat Satellite 6.18.11 for RHEL 9 includes critical vulnerabilities that may allow attackers to take control of satellite services. These flaws are rated CVSS 9.0+, providing remote code execution paths that bypass authentication and enable full administrative access. Apply the vendor’s patch immediately and review satellite configuration to enforce least‑privilege access controls.

item.title: Red Hat Satellite 6.16.15 Async Update Released
item.description: Red Hat Satellite 6.16.15 for RHEL 8 and RHEL 9 receives an async update addressing multiple vulnerabilities. The update mitigates unspecified security issues with a CVSS base score listed in the CVE references, potentially preventing unauthorized access or privilege escalation. Administrators should apply the new Satellite package immediately to maintain system integrity.

item.title: OpenStack Platform 17.1 Manila Update Released
item.description: Red Hat OpenStack Platform 17.1 (Wallaby) receives a critical security update for the openstack-manila component. The patch addresses multiple vulnerabilities with CVSS scores listed in the CVE references, potentially allowing unauthorized data access or service disruption. Deploy the updated openstack-manila package promptly to secure storage services.

item.title: PostgreSQL security update fixes 52 vulnerabilities, ends support for PostgreSQL 14
item.description: The PostgreSQL Global Development Group released PostgreSQL 18.7, 17.12, 16.16, 15.20 and 14.25 on November 12, fixing 52 security vulnerabilities and more than 140 other bugs. Most of those code execution bugs are memory errors or type confusion, where PostgreSQL handles a value as the wrong data type.

item.title: SCKit Worm Targets MSPs via ScreenConnect
item.description: A worm-like malware toolkit named SCKit has been deployed in recent ScreenConnect attacks against managed service providers. The malware spreads from infected customer devices to MSP technicians' computers, enabling attackers to compromise additional managed networks and exfiltrate data. Security teams should isolate affected systems, update ScreenConnect to the latest version, and monitor for lateral movement.

item.title: Hackers Exploit 4,800 GitHub Accounts for Cloud Credentials
item.description: A wfx-loot campaign compromised 4,837 GitHub accounts, using them to scan 61,764 repositories, open pull requests, and deploy secrets‑stealing malware. The attackers leveraged credential reuse and automated scanning to exfiltrate cloud service keys, exposing multiple cloud environments to unauthorized access. GitHub has issued a security advisory, urging users to rotate compromised credentials, enable two‑factor authentication, and review repository access logs.

item.title: Arctic Wolf Discusses Agentic AI in Security Ops
item.description: Arctic Wolf released a report on how agentic AI and human analysts collaborate to accelerate security operations, reduce investigation time, and improve threat response. The document details AI-driven automation integrated with expert analysis to streamline incident detection, triage, and remediation, citing performance metrics.

item.title: Feds Seize $1.2B from Binance Theft, Takedown FaceStealer Tools
item.description: The DOJ and FBI seized $1.2 billion tied to a North Korea‑linked cryptocurrency theft and dismantled FaceStealer malware tools. Investigations revealed the funds were proceeds from stolen digital assets, while the takedown removed the credential‑harvesting infrastructure. Cryptocurrency exchanges are urged to strengthen monitoring and compliance to deter future thefts and cooperate with ongoing investigations.

item.title: Chrome Early Stable Update 158.0.8127.36/37 for Windows
item.description: Google Chrome released an early stable update for Windows, version 158.0.8127.36/37, as part of its routine patch cycle. The update includes minor bug fixes and performance improvements, with a full changelog available in the release notes. Users are advised to install the update promptly to maintain compatibility and benefit from the latest stability enhancements.

item.title: Apache HTTP Server Vulnerabilities Enable Potential Code Execution
item.description: Apache HTTP Server’s mod_dav, mod_vhost_alias, and mod_md modules contain memory corruption flaws that allow attackers to crash or potentially execute code via crafted WebDAV locks or specific requests. CVE-2026-109163’s stack buffer overflow can lead to arbitrary code execution, while CVE-2026-42528 and CVE-2026-109163 also enable denial of service. Administrators should apply patches and restrict WebDAV access until the fixes are deployed.

item.title: CVE-2026-126793 - Privilege escalation in Aurora PostgreSQL dialect detection in AWS Advanced Go Wrapper
item.description: Bulletin ID: 2026-182-AWS Publication Date: 11/12/2026 13:00 PM PST Description: An untrusted search path issue in Aurora PostgreSQL dialect detection in the AWS Advanced Go Wrapper from release 2026-04-06 (awssql/v2.0.0) and before release 2026-07-29 (awssql/v2.0.3) could allow a remote authenticated user to escalate privileges to those of another database user, including a member of the rds_superuser role, via a crafted function that runs when that user connects to an Aurora PostgreSQL cluster through an affected version of the wrapper.

item.title: Debian-LAN ACL flaw allows credential changes
item.description: A flaw in Debian-LAN’s Kerberos admin server ACLs permits authenticated users to alter other users’ credentials, enabling privilege escalation. The vulnerability stems from overly permissive ACL configuration, lacking proper access checks, and could be exploited by insiders with valid credentials. Red Hat recommends applying the latest Debian-LAN patch or tightening ACLs to restrict admin server access, mitigating potential credential tampering.

item.title: x11vnc Shared Memory Permission Flaw
item.description: The x11vnc remote desktop server creates shared memory segments with insecure permissions, exposing a local privilege escalation vector. A local attacker could read sensitive data or alter screen contents, potentially compromising user sessions and data integrity. Apply the vendor patch or upgrade to the latest x11vnc release to enforce proper memory permissions.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Outlook, Exchange Online and Teams
item.description: Microsoft says failed server health checks disrupted Outlook and other Microsoft 365 services. The company is still investigating the cause and has disclosed no evidence of a cyberattack.

item.title: TigerVNC Stores TLS Exceptions as Trusted CAs
item.description: TigerVNC viewer treats TLS certificate exceptions as trusted CAs, allowing a remote attacker to impersonate any VNC server after a user accepts an exception. The flaw requires user interaction and does not grant code execution, yet it enables man‑in‑the‑middle attacks on VNC sessions. Ubuntu advises upgrading to TigerVNC 1.2.0 or later and avoiding unverified certificate acceptance.

item.title: Still in the Meeting: BlueNoroff Six Months On
item.description: In April, Arctic Wolf Labs documented how BlueNoroff used fake Zoom and Microsoft Teams meetings, ClickFix prompts, and AI-generated participants to compromise leaders in the Web3 and cryptocurrency sector. We expected the threat actor to adapt after we published that report.

item.title: USN-9087-1: signing-party vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that the gpg-key2ps tool in signing-party did not properly sanitize user IDs before passing them to a shell. If a user were tricked into processing a specially crafted OpenPGP key, an attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary commands.

item.title: USN-9086-1: SA-Exim vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that SA-Exim unsafely evaluated the parameters of its greylisting SpamAssassin rule. An attacker able to write SpamAssassin configuration files or rules could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code.

item.title: USN-9085-1: Ruby OpenID vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that Ruby OpenID sent a request to the claimed identifier URL before verifying the signature of an OpenID response. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to perform server-side request forgery attacks.

item.title: USN-9084-1: Radicale vulnerability
item.description: It was discovered that Radicale did not delay failed authentication attempts when using htpasswd authentication. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to obtain user passwords through timing or brute-force attacks.

item.title: Gevent server flaw enables HTTP request smuggling
item.description: The gevent WSGI server fails to validate chunked transfer encoding trailers, enabling remote attackers to smuggle HTTP requests and potentially elevate privileges. Request smuggling can bypass security controls, leading to unauthorized data access or command execution. Upgrade to the latest gevent version or apply the vendor’s patch, and enforce strict trailer validation.

item.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Hits Outlook, Teams, Copilot
item.description: Microsoft is investigating a widespread outage that has disrupted Outlook, Microsoft Teams, and Copilot services for users worldwide. Preliminary diagnostics indicate a network routing issue within Microsoft’s global infrastructure, causing connectivity failures across multiple regions. Microsoft has deployed a temporary fix and is working to restore full functionality while monitoring for residual impact.

item.title: Chrome 159 Promoted to Beta Channel
item.description: Google Chrome promoted version 159 to the Beta channel for Windows, macOS, and Linux, expanding early access for developers and testers. The update includes under‑the‑hood performance and stability improvements alongside several new features, but no security vulnerabilities are reported. Users may switch channels via the Chrome settings or consult the Chromium blog for detailed change logs and bug‑reporting procedures.

The update fixes multiple vulnerabilities rated as Important, with CVSS scores available via referenced CVE links, and reduces privilege escalation risk. Customers should apply the patch promptly to prevent potential denial‑of‑service or privilege escalation and mitigate related risks.

item.title: Luna Moth Targets Law Firms with Token Theft
item.description: Extortion group Luna Moth re‑targets law firms that declined its first ransom, launching a social‑engineering campaign to harvest Microsoft access tokens. The attack leverages phishing emails that embed malicious attachments or links, exploiting user credential theft to gain privileged cloud access. Security teams should enforce multi‑factor authentication, monitor token usage, and conduct employee awareness training to mitigate token‑based credential compromise.

item.title: Sudo Time Restriction Bypass Vulnerability
item.description: Sudo on Ubuntu 18.04 LTS and 20.04 LTS contains a flaw that fails to enforce NOTBEFORE and NOTAFTER time restrictions when timestamps lack a timezone indicator. A local attacker could manipulate the TZ environment variable to execute commands outside the intended time window, escalating privileges. Ubuntu has released updates for both releases; administrators should apply them to prevent the bypass.

item.title: N‑Able Zero‑Day Exploited for Miner Deployment
item.description: Hackers are exploiting a newly disclosed N‑Able N‑Central zero‑day, dubbed '4EverAble2Shell', to compromise servers and deploy cryptocurrency miners. The flaw permits unauthenticated remote code execution, enabling attackers to gain root access even on systems that have applied the latest emergency hotfix. N‑Able has released a patch; administrators should immediately apply the update and monitor for unauthorized miner processes.

item.title: United Airlines Bans AI Assistants for Credential Safety
item.description: United Airlines has prohibited customers from using AI assistants to access its services, citing risks of credential exposure and transactions. The decision follows concerns that shared login tokens could be harvested by malicious actors, enabling unauthorized account activity and data leakage. Customers are advised to use official mobile apps and two‑factor authentication, and airlines will monitor for suspicious account behavior.

item.title: Red Hat Issues Critical Fence‑Agents Update
item.description: Red Hat released a critical security update for fence‑agents on RHEL 9.8 EUS, addressing multiple high‑impact vulnerabilities. The update mitigates remote code execution risks by patching underlying flaws identified in the fence‑agents component, with CVSS base scores indicating severe impact. Administrators should apply the RHSA‑2026:99693 update immediately and verify that fence‑agents is running the latest patched version.

item.title: Apache HTTP/2 Module Vulnerability Allows Remote Code Execution
item.description: Apache HTTP Server's HTTP/2 module contains a critical flaw that permits unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability, which lacks a CVE identifier, could allow attackers to run arbitrary code on affected servers without credentials. Apache has released an update; administrators should apply the patch immediately and verify that HTTP/2 traffic is properly secured.

item.title: Maersk Reports Legacy System Cyber Incident
item.description: Maersk disclosed a cyber incident that impacted its legacy system, adding to a series of attacks on shipping ports worldwide. The event follows a ransomware attack on Brazil’s largest port last week, highlighting persistent threats to maritime infrastructure. Maritime operators should review legacy system security, apply available patches, and strengthen monitoring to mitigate future incidents.

item.title: ThreatsDay: 59 Linux Kernel Bugs, Falcon Spyware, GSocket Backdoors + 17 More Stories
item.description: A search result isn't always safe. An access request isn't always harmless. Attackers are using fake websites, stolen access, and trusted tools to get into places they shouldn't be.

item.title: New SignDrop Zero-Day Exploit Turns Windows CLFS Security Feature Into SYSTEM Access
item.description: Public exploit code released earlier this week claims that a local Windows user can gain SYSTEM privileges through the Common Log File System driver. The proof of concept, called SignDrop, targets a log-authentication feature added to the driver last year.
